title: Daily Market Digest: October 31, 2026
subtitle: Review of Friday, October 30, 2026, Trading Session

items.headline: Tech Sell-Off Drags Major Indices Lower Amid AI Spending Concerns
items.summary: U.S. equities closed sharply lower on Friday, October 30, 2026, marking the worst day since June for the Nasdaq and S&P 500. A widespread sell-off in technology stocks was fueled by disappointing corporate earnings and mounting investor worries that significant investments in artificial intelligence might not yield expected returns. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite recorded its steepest monthly decline since March 2025.

items.headline: Intel Plummets on Weak Guidance
items.summary: Intel ($INTC) shares plunged 28.58% to $65.76, marking its worst day since 1974. The steep decline followed a forecast for fourth-quarter sales that fell below analysts' expectations, citing ongoing weakness in the PC market and concerns over AI investment returns.

items.headline: Solowin Holdings Drops on Reverse Split
items.summary: Solowin Holdings ($AXG) saw a significant decline of 44.73% to $2.05, attributed to a 1-for-200 reverse stock split.

items.headline: Grid Dynamics Holdings Surges
items.summary: Grid Dynamics Holdings ($GDYN) was among the top gainers, soaring 40.8% to $13.36.

items.headline: Regeneron Pharma Rises on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals ($REGN) shares rose 13.33% to $926.96 following a report of stronger-than-expected third-quarter profits.

items.headline: Energy Leads, Tech Lags in Friday's Session
items.summary: The Energy sector emerged as the top-performing sector on Friday, gaining 1.91%. This was driven by stronger-than-expected profits from oil giants like ExxonMobil ($XOM), which climbed 2.2%, and Chevron ($CVX), up 1.8%. Conversely, Information Technology was the weakest sector, falling 4.24%, as concerns about AI spending and weaker earnings from major tech players weighed heavily on investor sentiment.

items.headline: Q3 GDP Growth Strong, but Inflationary Pressures Persist
items.summary: The U.S. economy expanded at an annualized rate of 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026 (July-September), an increase from 2.2% in the prior quarter. This growth was largely attributed to robust consumer spending and significant investments by AI companies in data centers. However, inflation remains a concern, with the PCE index rising 0.5% in September, its largest increase in six months, pushing the yearly rate to 3.6% and further from the Federal Reserve's 2% target.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady, Future Hikes Possible
items.summary: The Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate target range at 3.75% to 4% after a September hike, though two officials reportedly advocated for another increase. Higher long-term interest rates are primarily influenced by investor expectations of stronger nominal growth and elevated neutral interest rates, suggesting the Fed may still have work to do on monetary policy.

items.headline: Next Week's Watch: Apple and AMD Earnings
items.summary: Investors will be closely watching next week's earnings calendar, with major reports expected from Apple ($AAPL) on Monday and AMD ($AMD) on Tuesday, leading a series of releases from significant U.S. companies.
